mainText:
Good morning, it's Saturday, Oct. 31,

North Korea is suspected to be behind largest-ever crypto heist.
Experts say an elite North Korean hacking unit appears to be behind a hack that stole roughly $6.3B from Binance, the world's largest
cryptocurrency
exchange. Binance said it believes hackers breached its systems from multiple points of attack in what it describes as a "complex hack." The exchange is working with the FBI and Secret Service to recover stolen assets, but analysts estimate roughly $2.4B may be unrecoverable. The exchange has pledged to cover all customer losses.
President Donald Trump to rally in Kansas and Iowa tomorrow.
The Republican president reversed his decision to cancel back-to-back rallies in the two states, both of which have competitive Senate races. The shuffling comes as early voting in Iowa and Kansas has surged roughly 30% compared with 2022, raising questions about whether Republicans maintain an edge. Trump is also hosting about 20 tele-rallies this weekend.

midterm elections in the US
Christa Pike releases first public statement since botched execution.
Pike, 50, said she is in constant mental and physical pain and struggles to speak after surviving a lethal injection in Tennessee last month. She blamed the failed execution on "incompetence," while thanking the medical workers who attended to her in the aftermath. Pike's attorneys have urged Tennessee Gov. Bill Lee to reduce her sentence to life in prison.
Police investigate former Prince Andrew and Epstein activities at royal estate.
Scottish authorities confirmed they are conducting active inquiries following allegations that the former prince, Jeffrey Epstein, and Ghislaine Maxwell trafficked women to Balmoral Castle. The US Justice Department previously released photos of Andrew and Epstein shooting at the royal residence, which is where Queen Elizabeth II died in 2022. King Charles currently owns the property.
Scientists identify meteorite found in Sahara as 4.1-billion-year-old piece of Mars.
A NASA study has determined that a nearly two-pound, rose-colored meteorite discovered in Mali's Sahara desert came from Mars (
see 101
). It is one of the three most ancient Martian meteorites on Earth, providing rare insight into how the red planet's crust formed as magma cooled and then changed upon contact with subsurface water. The data suggests Mars may have had a more dynamic water cycle than previously believed.
Linguists rediscover earliest spoken audio of Louisiana's dying Creole language.
Recorded in New Orleans in 1935, the audio offers a rare perspective on a language largely studied through written records. Enslaved Africans developed the language in the 18th century, blending French with West African grammar and incorporating Native American words for unfamiliar plants and animals. The people in the recordings include a retired police officer, schoolteachers, and a pianist.
